correctness.rationale: Linear Zimin words are squarefree by induction using their unique largest letter. In \(Z_mZ_m\) the only square containing \(m\) is the whole double, and every other square lies in its middle \(Z_{m-1}Z_{m-1}\), yielding exact starts and half-lengths by induction. The circular word has one copy of \(n\), so squares avoid it and occur only in the opposite double \(Z_{n-1}Z_{n-1}\). A unique square of half-length \(2^k-1\) survives a rotation cut exactly when \(2^k-1\le c\le (2^n-1)-(2^k-1)\). Nesting proves the histogram. The next letter \(k+1\) differs from the initial \(1\), excluding higher fractional powers. Independent exhaustive computations to \(n=11\) and direct rotations to \(n=8\) corroborate all critical steps.

value.rationale: The exact cyclic-square factor spectrum, unique squarefree rotation and complete exponential-stratified cut histogram jointly resolve natural repetition invariants of the canonical recursively nested Zimin family. They explain how a linearly squarefree word hides all nontrivial squares solely at wraparound and quantify every cut, beyond a trivial existence/nonexistence check. The general all-order structural classification is mathematically motivated in circular pattern matching and power-avoidance research.
